proof_summary: After dividing the inclusion–exclusion formula by \((n-1)!\), the fixed-\(k\) inner sum is asymptotic to \(2^k n^k/k!\) (only its \(j=0\) term contributes at leading order), while \((n-1)_k\sim n^k\), so the normalized summands tend to \((-2)^k/k!\). A summable exponential majorant permits passage of the limit through the sum, giving \(e^{-2}\); separately, the correction sum tends to zero and \(n!/(n-2)\sim(n-1)!\), so both expressions have the same asymptotic.
